newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Timor car sales strong despite dispute.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Timor car sales strong despite dispute.

text.p: A new, cut-price car sold in Indonesia, the Timor, which Japan has threatened to challenge in a trade complaint, has been generating 400 customer orders per week, the car company said on Thursday.
PT Timor Putra Nasional spokesman Mohamad Ircham said sales of the Timor sedan could hit 50,000 by next July.
On Wednesday, Tokyo announced it planned to complain to the World Trade Organization that Indonesia was giving special tax breaks to promote sales of the car.
The Timor currently is being made in South Korea and imported, but is eventually to be manufactured in Indonesia.
PT Timor Putra Nasional is a joint venture between President Suharto's youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra, and Kia Motors of South Korea.

Ircham said more than 8,500 Indonesians had already paid 3.5 million rupiah ($1,507) each to reserve a four-door, 1,600cc Timor sedan since order books opened on July 8. The Timor officially went on sale on October 1, sparking the Japanese complaint.
"The most optimistic target for all of Indonesia in the first year to July 1997 is 50,000 cars, and the most pessimistic target is 35,000 cars," Ircham told Reuters in an interview.
PT Timor has said it plans to build 200,000 units a year by 1998-99 and to have constructed one million cars before 2003.
The first cars, imported fully built from KIA, started to arrive on the Jakarta docks in August.
Ircham said that of more than 4,000 vehicles already landed, 350 had been delivered as of Wednesday to the 10 official dealerships in the greater Jakarta area.
"In the next phase from March 1997, we will assemble them here in cooperation the PT Indomobil (in Jakarta) and PT Indauda (in Surabaya)," he said.
"Then we will move in the direction of full manufacturing when our factory in Cikampek (West Java) is finished in 1998," he said.
Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said Japan planned to file a complaint with the WTO over the issue "within a week or so."
"There is a strong suspicion that Indonesia's national car policy contravenes WTO rules," government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters on Wednesday.
In Jakarta, Indonesian Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo replied that Indonesia was ready to argue its case.
"We are ready to face the WTO," he told reporters.
Japan's MITI said Indonesia had not imposed any tariffs on its "national" cars produced in South Korea when they passed through Indonesian customs.
"As soon as we confirm the number and sales price of these cars, we will start the procedures for filing a complaint to the WTO within a week or so," a ministry official said.
Ircham said the Timor was selling in Jakarta for 35 million rupiah ($15,067), including on-the-road costs.

The price is significantly cheaper than similar models in the Indonesian market, which is dominated by Japanese car makers. Toyota Motor Corp's popular Corolla, for example, sells for around 69 million rupiah.
